minutes.headline: Board reviewed two park concepts for 30 School Street and heard a recommended FY2023 capital plan.
minutes.summary: The Select Board heard a landscape architect present two concept plans for the old primary school site at 30 School Street. Members and residents leaned toward option A with seat-wall elements and wanted more parking. The town manager presented a recommended FY2023 capital plan, the board approved minutes, reviewed legislative priorities, and adjourned.

what_happened.line: The Select Board heard a landscape architect present two concept plans for the old primary school site at 30 School Street; members and residents leaned toward option A.
The board set February 15 for its next session with the landscape architect and chose to post options A and B online for comment instead of a second survey.
The town manager presented a recommended FY2023 capital plan: thirty requests, with 20 recommended for funding from tax revenue, free cash and unexpended capital.
The board approved minutes, reviewed legislative priorities including the Flat Hill Road culvert and old primary school abatement, and adjourned.
The chair told a resident the senior tax relief effort would not be ready for annual town meeting.

why_it_matters: The capital plan is a list of requests paid from taxes and free cash, so the 20 recommended items are what residents will likely be asked to vote on at town meeting.
The park design for 30 School Street is still open for comment, including the parking question raised by residents, and nothing was voted.
Senior tax relief will not be on the annual town meeting warrant, so it cannot reach that vote this year.
watch_next: February 15 Select Board meeting with the landscape architect; materials due three days ahead.
Online posting of options A and B for 30 School Street, open for public comment.
